quest.title: Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame
quest.description: The film's shooting is going smoothly. The story recorded in the Kamera seems to be being performed somewhere beyond the frame...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame

talks.objective: Go to Hotel Debord to film

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayaka! Yoimiya! You're already here!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Good morning. Xavier said yesterday afternoon went well?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! And how about you, Ayaka? What were you up to yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: After we split up, Ayato went to see Iudex Neuvillette at the Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I was originally thinking of going with him, but he said he could manage it himself. He told me to go see the sights around Fontaine and to enjoy the local culture.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: So, I rode the aquabus with Yoimiya and visited the opera house on Erinnyes island.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yeah, you wouldn't believe what we saw there! Two mechanical puppets that were dancing together! You've already seen them, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Dirge of Coppelia...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And the Nemesis of Coppelius...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yeah, yeah, those two! Amazing, aren't they?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: We sat and watched for quite a while. It was mesmerizing, like we could keep watching them forever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it was the same for us the first time we saw them, too.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Afterwards, we went swimming at the beach! Well, diving to be exact... It was the first time I ever breathed underwater!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I held Ayaka's hand and we counted down together... Three, two, one... And then, "splash!" we were beneath the waves.

talks.objective: Go to Hotel Debord to film

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: At first, I didn't dare to open my mouth. But once I couldn't hold my breath any longer, I decided to take a big breath in. Hehe, turns out the water wasn't as salty as I imagined... It didn't really taste like anything at all!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Before I knew it, I was breathing like normal down there! It was an amazing feeling! Ayaka said I was too nervous and needed to loosen my grip. She got used to everything way faster than I did!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: #I knew that {NICKNAME} could do it, so I had no doubt we could do it, too. That helped me feel at ease as soon as we dove in.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: The underwater world in Fontaine truly is beautiful. I loved seeing the Romaritime Flowers blossoming underwater, like little candles lighting up the streets at night.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yeah, and there are so many creatures that we've never seen in Inazuma!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Like those fish that shimmer like a sword blade... Whoosh! Oh, and those big fish that call when they see people... "Woooo"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Hunter's Rays and Blubberbeasts!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, I just love the name Blubberbeast. Just wait till Pops and the others hear about this, they probably won't believe a word I say!

talks.objective: Go to Hotel Debord to film

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yoimiya was down there for quite a while. It was dark before we finally rode the aquabus back to the city. I figured she'd wanna sleep in today.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yeah, even I was worried that I wouldn't be able to get up! I still felt like I was drifting in the waves when I went to sleep last night.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: But as soon as I woke up today, I remembered that we'd all be shooting a film together, and I was ready to go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of the film, where's everybody else?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: My brother and Xavier were speaking to the restaurant owner about using the place as a filming location, they should be here soon.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: As for the others, they...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: We're here.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Please excuse my tardiness. I just finished the Special Patrol's six-mile morning jog.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, six miles!?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *yawn* I'm so tired... I heard you all chatting, so I decided to come down. I sure could use some of that endless energy everyone else has...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Good morning, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Morning... Can someone fetch me a cup of coffee? More milk, hold the sugar.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Sure, I'd be happy to do that for you.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: No. You can't go anywhere. Please have a seat over here so I can get started on your makeup. The last thing I want is coffee stains on my costumes.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I can get the coffee! It's the perfect job for an assistant!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So much energy... Seriously, what's her secret?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Yoimiya's always like that. But you sure look exhausted, Furina. It's because you're not used to waking up so early, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course not! I spent the whole night reading the novel from cover to cover, marking sections that either need to be omitted or adapted.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Paimon didn't expect you to be so thorough!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Heh, well, I was the biggest star in all of Fontaine, after all. It takes more than just a pretty face to earn a reputation like that. I know how to get serious when the situation calls for it.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I went all out when I was acting as an archon, so why wouldn't I do the same for my own life?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Here's your coffee, Director Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you. Ah, the sound of being called "Director" and the aroma of coffee... feels almost as refreshing as hearing the birds chirping in the morning.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: It seems everyone has managed to arrive on time.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: We've reached an agreement with the restaurant owner. We are free to use the second floor to shoot our film.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: He is really looking forward to our film, and hopes that providing his restaurant as a filming location will attract more customers.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Well then, Mr. Xavier. I'll leave the rest to you.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Okay, thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: First, I'd like to introduce our new members...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: This is our prop manager, Veronique. She'll be in charge of all the film's props and items.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: And this is Bonnot, our lighting technician. He'll be in charge of lighting and illumination to set up each scene's atmosphere.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, sure feels like we have some real professionals joining the crew now!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: First of all, please allow me to first express my sincerest gratitude to everyone in the crew.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: When my investor informed me yesterday that he wouldn't be able to provide the funds, I really thought that was the nail in the coffin for this film.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I had no idea that I'd find so many people willing to help me on such short notice. Thank you... Thank you all, from the bottom of my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: No need to be so cordial, Mr. Xavier. We are all honored to be a part of this.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Your works made a profound impression on me when I saw them back in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I am sure that someday, this film will be remembered as a prime example of cultural exchange between Fontaine and Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yes, the story is the reason I agreed to join. I can't bear to even imagine what this film would look like without the very best director.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Anyway, I would like to make a promise to everyone... That as the producer of this film, I'll do whatever I can to ensure that everything goes as smoothly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: This is not just my film. It also embodies the thoughts and feelings of every person here, as well as the endless effort we are about to pour into it!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: So, without further ado... "The Two Musketeers" will officially begin filming now!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: You may take it from here, Director Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright. Listen up, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The first scene takes place when the two young musketeers are living at the baron's home, still unaware of all that is about to happen to them. We'll need props and lighting to set the scene. Our lead actors can go get their makeup done, and extras, please take this time to go over your positions...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, seems Furina's really kicking things into gear as the director.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Is everyone clear? I don't want anyone traipsing around the set like Umbrellafinches.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, Kameras will start rolling as soon as the set is ready! Let's make a film that'll make some serious waves in Fontaine!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh... not the kind of waves that drown everyone, I mean the good kind of waves...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, it seems like she's still a bit traumatized by that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's go see if there's anything we can do to help!

talks.objective: Look for the people who need help

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ayaka has mentioned you to me before. She said that you two were great friends when you were kids.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: No talking. I'm thinking about how to do your eyeshadow.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Ah yes, to help me really look the part.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: To achieve a more... young and naive look for this scene.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Are you saying the wrinkles around my eyes are too deep?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: You just have too much of a calculating look in your eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Hah, you sure don't mince your words. It seems you really haven't changed much.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...Quiet.

talks.objective: Look for the people who need help

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: How about here?

dialogues.speaker: Bonnot
dialogues.text: Hmm... A little more to the left.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You got it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Yoimiya, do you need a hand?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No, no, I'm fine! Y'know, doing the lighting is kinda like designing a fireworks show. It's interesting to imagine what kind of atmosphere the lights will create!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #I heard that {NICKNAME} will be operating the Kamera, and Paimon will be the clapper loader, right? Hehe, those roles are just perfect for the two of you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Is that because it'll be easy for Paimon to hold the clapperboard while flying?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Well, sure, there's that... But that's not exactly what I meant.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I just think that after all your journeys together, you two must have developed a super close bond, and just naturally know how to work with each other! If I'm not mistaken, the director will want the Kameras rolling as soon as the clapperboard goes "clack"!

choices.text: Actually, we start rolling before that.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, I see! Haha, it's amazing to see the magic behind filmmaking!

response.speaker: Bonnot
response.text: Yoimiya, we need lights over there, too!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh! On it!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I've gotta get back to work, chat with ya later. Oh, it's exciting to see so many people working together to bring the film to life!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like Yoimiya's really getting into it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But she was right, {NICKNAME}, we do have a super close bond, don't we?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon's really happy to hear that!

choices.text: The clapperboard just gets edited out in post-production.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: So is this a real musket?

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: No, it's just a prop weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Not bad. Have you seen a real musket before?

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: Only in books and newspapers. I made this one based on the relative shape and proportions I saw in reference images.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: When we're filming, some special gunpowder will be applied around the muzzle, which will help create the flash and smoke effects of a real gun being fired.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Which means it'll be up to the actors to portray the recoil.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: That's right. The sound effects for gunshots will also be added in post-production.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Thank you, Veronique. I think I know where to start now.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: However, the muskets' gears and firing pin could still use some work. Adding some wear on the metallic components will make them appear more realistic.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Also, be sure to rub the muskets with some oil each time before we start shooting. That will give the impression that the firearms have been well-maintenanced.

dialogues.speaker: Veronique
dialogues.text: Good point!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: You seem to know a lot, Miss Chevreuse. I assume you use these types of firearms on a regular basis?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes, I perform routine maintenance on my weapons every day. Just like we as people need to eat and sleep, muskets need to be cleaned and maintained.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I also perform similar care for my sword every day, and familiarize myself with its shape and weight... to the point where it feels like a natural extension of my body.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes. This way, our weapons will never betray us in the heat of battle.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes, well said. It seems we have the same philosophy on this topic.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, sounds like they've found a common interest to talk about.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Though these props differ from the muskets I use, I can still give you some pointers.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Good, I look forward to your instruction.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: First and foremost, never point the weapon at anyone, regardless of whether it's a real or prop weapon, or whether you're holding it or it's on the table. This holds for any time when you're not actively engaging an enemy.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Okay, understood.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: When aiming the musket, extend your arm so that it is level with your shoulder, and use your eye to look down the weapon's sights.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Like this?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Not bad. Now, try saying your lines.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: ...This is the end of the road for you.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Good, now turn your body a little. That way, you will give your enemy less of a target to work with... And relax your shoulders. Here, allow me to demonstrate.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...This is the end of the road for you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Excuse me, Miss Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Director Furina, there's something I wish to discuss with you.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Like this?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes, much better.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: ...What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Mhm, I do see your point. But are you sure you wish to do this?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I believe it would be most fitting.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, if you insist... Alright, I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ahem! Miss Ayaka, Miss Chevreuse, could the two of you please come over here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on? Are we gonna start filming now?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Let's go see.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I have a question for you, Miss Chevreuse. Would you be willing to play the role of a musketeer?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: To clarify, I would like to turn over my role to Miss Chevreuse.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: But, brother...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Ayaka. I actually view this as a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I was becoming troubled trying to set aside some time to speak to the staff at the Palais Mermonia. I would like to have some conversations about the cultural exchange between our two countries, and I've heard that the bureaucratic process here can get rather complicated.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Now, I will be able to focus on my work. Besides, you also know that I'm not really one for public performances.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: ...Are you really sure?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: From a director's point of view, I also felt like the relationship between the two musketeers in the original story could be improved.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The older brother in the story plays the lead role with his overbearing character. But this causes his character to overshadow that of his sister, and the theme of the two supporting and relying on each other isn't conveyed very well.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: But if we were to change the siblings to two sisters of a similar age... then that aspect of the story might come through more clearly.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Also, I've seen you instructing Ayaka. That cold and dignified personality is exactly what we need for the older musketeer.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Of course, even with all of these insights, the decision should still be made by Miss Chevreuse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chevreuse mentioned that she really likes this story, right? Paimon bets that she'll take the role.

choices.text: But she will still have to prioritize her work.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Alright, I'll take the role.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Good, it's decided then. I'll get started on making edits to the script.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: We'll also need to make some immediate adjustments to the lighting, props, and costumes.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah, I have a feeling that our adaptation will be even better than the original story!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: You're doing a great favor for me, Miss Chevreuse. You have my gratitude.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Don't mention it. I like this character, so if anything, I should be the one thanking you.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Well, since my brother is the one who brought up the idea, I suppose there's no need to worry.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Let's go, Miss Chevreuse. I look forward to working with you.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Please, just call me Chevreuse.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Seems like you're really going out of your way to solve the problem I was having with your makeup.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Surely you jest, Chiori. I assure you that I was mostly motivated by a desire to spend more time on formal business.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Oh come on, you really think I'd buy that? According to what I've heard from Ayaka, her brother is someone who can juggle ten different matters at the same time. I'm sure you have other reasons for backing out.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: #Perhaps. Ayaka always said she wanted to go out and see more of the world, just like {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: But I feel that she needs not only to see other nations, but also to make some different kinds of friends. I think it would be harder for her to make new connections with me constantly by her side... I would like to give her some space.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Alright, go on, spoil her some more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ayato! It's too bad you're stepping down from the role... Paimon really wanted to see you act as a musketeer.

choices.text: "This is the punishment you deserve!"

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Heh, no need to poke fun at me. I'd wager that you also felt that I wasn't the best candidate for the role.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, it's a little hard for Paimon to imagine you saying those lines.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So are you going to go back to work now?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Yes, I've made an appointment to meet some people from the Palais Mermonia. Now, I will have some more time to prepare.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, get the Kamera ready! Paimon, get the clapperboard! Actors, to your positions! We're about to start shooting the first scene!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Go on, now. And please take good care of Ayaka.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, don't worry!

choices.text: You can count on us.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Thank you. I look forward to seeing the film when it's finished.

choices.text: Good luck with your work.
"This is justice!"
But we still don't know if she's a big fan of acting.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, now that we're all here, let me help set the scene for everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The first scene takes place when our two main characters are still living at the baron's estate. They've been ostracized and verbally abused by others in the household, but they still have no idea why. We want to capture how naive and innocent they are, despite their pain.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Chevreuse will be playing the role of the older sister, Tulipe, and Ayaka will be the younger sister, Iris. Be sure to get close-ups of the main characters at the right moment.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Silence on the set! Lights, Kamera, action!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's gooooo!

dialogues.speaker: "Iris"
dialogues.text: Tulipe, mother's been out for quite a while now.

dialogues.speaker: "Tulipe"
dialogues.text: Perhaps she went to pick some flowers on the way home. You know how she loves flowers.

dialogues.speaker: "Rain"
dialogues.text: Iris, Tulipe! I'm home.

choices.text: (Zoom in for a close shot with the mother.)

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: ...Mother! You were out for so long, we were beginning to worry about you.

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: I'm sorry, but I'm back now, safe and sound... Here, I've brought your favorite treat, apple turnovers.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Mother... what are those bruises on your hand?

choices.text: (Zoom in for a close-up on the mother.)

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: Huh? What bruises? Oh... I must have bumped into something while I was working yesterday.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: But I didn't notice them this morning.

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: Then perhaps they're from when I accidentally tripped when I was out just now.

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: By the way, did you have fun playing at home?

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: What's the matter, Iris?

choices.text: (Focus on Iris.)

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Well... we've realized that... no one really wants to play with us.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: They even took Iris' doll, and spat at us.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: And they even called us names... They said we were...

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: Shh... It's alright, don't worry. Girls, listen to me...

choices.text: (Pan over all three characters.)

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: It doesn't matter what anyone says... don't listen to them. No one can define you with such words.

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: You both have wonderful lives ahead of you. Just like your names... you will both blossom like beautiful flowers.

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: Maybe your time to blossom hasn't quite come yet, but one day, you two will bloom more beautifully than anything else.

response.speaker: "Rain"
response.text: Don't let the soil you're in now ruin your future beauty, understand? My dear daughters...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...And cut!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Not bad... The actors' emotions were all on point, let's keep that take.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Also, if our clapper loader could avoid shouting at the start of the scene next time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... Got it...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Whew... Great. I was a little worried that my nerves would get the better of me. What about you, Chevreuse?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I felt fine, the lines weren't too difficult at all. Seems like Furina must have adapted the role nicely.

response.speaker: Elain
response.text: Hehe, you two were great. I couldn't tell it was your first time acting in a film. You should have more confidence!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Thank you for your encouragement.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Positions, everyone! We'll move on to the next scene after we try a few more Kamera angles.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everything proceeds at a great pace, and once Furina has adjusted some details to her satisfaction, you begin to film the second scene...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: This scene is when our two characters return home only to discover their mother has been murdered. Ready? Lights, Kamera, action!

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Mother, we're back.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: ...Mother?

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: What's wrong, Tulipe?

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Iris, stay away!

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Huh? Why? What's...

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: *gasp* Mother!

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Mother... she's...

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: There's poison in this cup.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Huh, I could have sworn I've seen this kind of cup before...

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Argh... Those aristocrats... They didn't even try to cover up their actions!

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Iris, we need to leave this place.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: Leave? But now that Mother is gone... where can we even go?

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Anywhere. All I know is that we can't stay in this house.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: But... are we just going to let them get away with this...?

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: We'll have our revenge, I promise you... just not right now.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: ...C'mon, let's go.

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: No, wait...

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: We can't just leave Mother here like this. At least... At least let me leave this rose with her...

response.speaker: "Iris"
response.text: That's why we went out in the first place... to buy her this flower.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: ...Alright.

response.speaker: "Tulipe"
response.text: Goodbye, Mother. We'll avenge you... someday.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: ...And cut!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Beautiful! Great performance!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh my, you're so amazing, Ayaka! And were those real tears I saw? How did you do it?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I was surprised, too.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Thank you for the kind compliments. Actually, as soon as Director Furina said "action," I told myself not to think about anything. I just felt the weight of the moment, and became the character.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: It's quite similar to practicing the art of the sword. You clear your mind and focus only on what's happening in front of you.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: (Ayaka's performance was amazing... Have I discovered an acting prodigy?)

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Pipe down, everyone. We need to move on to the next scene!

choices.text: (Zoom in for a close-up on each character.)
(Focus on the general surroundings.)
(Zoom in for a close-up on Tulipe.)
(Zoom out for a wide shot.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A full day of filming on the set quickly passes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Are we done already? But Paimon wants to keep playing with the clapperboard...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #How do you feel, {NICKNAME}? Is your arm sore from holding the Kamera all day?

choices.text: A little bit...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Good work, you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You too, Chevreuse. You were quite the actress today.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I've read this novel many times before. I have a good grasp of my character's mindset.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Anyway, do you remember my request from yesterday?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! We were having so much fun that Paimon nearly forgot...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You have a case where the murders seem really similar to the cases in the novel, right? So, uh... how are they similar, exactly?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: In the story, the main characters grow up to become the two musketeers, always using their guns to carry out their revenge.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: And on each of the victims, they'd place a Rainbow Rose as a signal that they've returned.

choices.text: So you mean...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Yes, that's correct. We've found Rainbow Roses just like in the novel. Seems like you're connecting the dots now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! That does sound pretty concerning...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Especially after seeing the script today. Now Paimon can't stop wondering what kind of ulterior motive the murderer might have...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? You're smart, Paimon wants to hear your thoughts.

choices.text: If we're only there to assist...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Good. On behalf of Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, thank you for your dedication to justice.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: There's no time to lose, we should start investigating right away. Follow me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Right now? But we just got done filming all day! Paimon's so tired...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The most valuable intel always comes after nightfall. They are like small, remote islands in the middle of the sea... if you don't stay vigilant, you will pass right by them in the fog.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: That's how one of my favorite books always puts it, at least.

choices.text: Then I think we can join the case.
There were Rainbow Roses in your case, too?
But it was a lot of fun.

talks.objective: Go to Leschots Clockwork Workshop to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Welcome to Leschots Clockwork Workshop. How can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hello. I'd like to know if anyone has purchased any special components lately.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Special components? Sorry, could you be more specific...?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I mean the kind of components that aren't typically used for clockwork toys, but for firearms.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Huh, for firearms? No, no, we don't sell those sort of things here...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Don't misunderstand, I'm not here to cause any trouble. We are merely investigating a case and we're hoping that you could cooperate.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: Well, to be completely honest, I'm not even sure what kind of components that would entail.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Has anyone ever purchased components here as an individual, rather than on behalf of an organization?

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: We have a lot of customers who buy toys, but those who buy components are all regular customers who buy in bulk on behalf of their organization.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Is that so? I understand. Thank you for your cooperation.

dialogues.speaker: Livre
dialogues.text: You're welcome, it's the least I can do.

talks.objective: Go to Beaumont Workshop to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Oh, hey Chevreuse! Run out of oil for your musket again?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hello, Estelle. I want to know if anyone has come to your shop recently to order some firearm components.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Oh, is this another case? Hmm, let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: I don't think so. Some people have requested that I make some prop guns for the Fontinalia Film Festival, but I refused all of those requests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Because there's no profit! I only make things here that can do some real heavy lifting. I don't have the energy to make some new molds just for the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Then, has anybody come specifically looking for mechanical components?

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Well, I usually sell off my scrap to the Fleuve Cendre. I don't typically give them to one specific person.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I understand. Thanks for your cooperation.

dialogues.speaker: Estelle
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. Always happy to have the Musketeers' patronage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like we haven't found any leads to go off yet.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yeah, unfortunately. Alright, let's head to Fleuve Cendre next.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you sure? Uh, people might not be so thrilled to see the captain of the Special Patrol there.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You think so, huh? Then I guess you don't know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Know what?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: That I grew up in Fleuve Cendre.

talks.objective: Go to the Fleuve Cendre to investigate

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's been a while, Tetreaux.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: Please, just get on with your request.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I want to know if you've heard anybody talking about muskets lately.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: Information isn't free, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I've heard that bandits have been extremely active in the countryside recently, and they've been affecting the delivery of goods to Poisson. I can allocate some more manpower to help out with that problem. What do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: Hehe, you're still as helpful as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: One of our men got drunk at dinner about a month ago, and lost his gun. Three days later, it turned up in the corner here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's weird about that? He just forgot where he put it, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: This is Fleuve Cendre, my friend. Anything of value left in the tavern won't ever make it to the next day.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: But that gun turned out to be an exception. It didn't get any new wear and tear on it, and didn't even appear to have been fired. We were quite mystified as to what could have happened.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I suspect it came back because the weapon was already known to the Gardes.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: You mean, a criminal was afraid the Marechaussee Phantom would use the shot marks to track them down? Maybe... But if that's the case, the culprit really took great care to avoid getting caught.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I didn't say anything about a criminal.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: In Fleuve Cendre, knowing who was killed is as easy as knowing what clothes you're wearing today.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: It's the guy living in the east side, isn't it? I've never liked him. Every time he's here, he just orders a drink and sits there with a nasty look in his eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So who was the one who lost the gun in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: Don't bother. Even if you ask, he wouldn't admit to owning a gun to some strangers, not to mention the captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: ...He's right.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: I know you grew up here, Chevreuse.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: Even though you're on good terms with the Spina, you've still been gone too long. Not many people know you here now, and a lot of people don't like the Special Patrol.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I know.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: So take my advice, and don't show your face too much around here. It's for your own safety.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I'll come and go as I please. And I'm afraid I'll be appearing more often due to my work.

dialogues.speaker: Tetreaux
dialogues.text: ...Alright, don't say I didn't warn ya.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hello, I'd like to ask some questions.

dialogues.speaker: Emerald
dialogues.text: I don't know anything.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'm not here to arrest anybody.

dialogues.speaker: Emerald
dialogues.text: You say that now...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: It's the truth. Here, take this as my guarantee.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, did Paimon just see what she thinks she saw? Is the captain of the Special Patrol bribing a citizen!?

choices.text: Shhh!

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: Seems you're different from the other Gardes.

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: What do you want to know?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Have you heard anything related to muskets in Fleuve Cendre lately? Anything at all...?

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: Muskets, huh... All I know is that about two weeks ago, we started hearing some loud noises at night... So loud, that it's been waking me up.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Were they gunshots?

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: Possibly, it's hard to tell around here.

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: Someone's house collapsing, a pipe exploding somewhere... it's all the same. But the noises I'm talking about definitely happened after I fell asleep.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Do you know where the noises were coming from?

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: I don't remember clearly...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Is it that you don't remember, or that you need to think about it some more?

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: You tell me.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Then please, think about it some more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? She's giving her even more Mora!

choices.text: I didn't see anything.

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: The noises came from the end of the southern waterway. I came out and had a look for myself when I wasn't sleeping well, but I didn't dare to get too close.

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: That's all I know.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Alright, I'll take your word for it.

response.speaker: Emerald
response.text: Thanks for the Pate de Fruit.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: No need to be surprised. I grew up here, remember? I know how to get people around here to talk.

choices.text: What talk?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Seems you catch on pretty quick.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Now then, let's keep going.

choices.text: I want some Pate de Fruit, too.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: My apologies. I'm all out of sweets.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Though, I do have some other tempting snacks in my custody — fries, fried chicken, and even onion rings.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But taking care of junk food is my responsibility. You're better off sticking to your normal, nutritious diet.

choices.text: Maybe she's just giving out some Pate de Fruit.
Keep your lips sealed and no one will ever know.
Besides, it's called "buying info."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's all this? Some broken planks and barrels, as well as some... liquor bottles?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes, but have a closer look, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Even though somebody has purposely tried to clean them up, these are obviously marks from musket bullets.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: In other words, someone was here trying to improve their shot. They were using the barrels and bottles for target practice.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, could it have been the killer!?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Your guess is as good as mine. Although many people at Fleuve Cendre own guns, few hide the fact from others, and even fewer would go to such lengths to hide markings from practice shots.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's go. There might be more to this.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Seems like that's all we'll be able to uncover for today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon feels like we managed to learn a lot more here than up on the surface!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes. Assuming that everything we found is indeed connected to our suspect, then their timeline was probably something like this...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: A month ago, our suspect found a gun and took it home to disassemble it. Once he'd figured out its mechanics, he brought it back.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: In the following weeks, he used some parts to create his own makeshift musket, and took it to the Fleuve Cendre for target practice.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Then, a few days ago, he found his target and carried out the murder. Once the deed was done, he left a Rainbow Rose on the body, just like the scene in the novel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, that all makes sense to Paimon, but we're still no closer to figuring out the killer's identity!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the guy who died...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The deceased was a resident of Fleuve Cendre. It's said that he was a poor, solitary man.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But if we're following the novel, shouldn't the guy have been a nobleman?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yeah... That's also something I'm trying to figure out.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: If we are indeed following the novel, and there's a story behind the murder, then his murder should be an act of vengeance. But according to our investigation, the deceased didn't have any enemies.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He was no saint, but no one's heard of a rival who hated him enough to shoot him dead, much less care to leave a rose on his body.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: What message is the killer trying to convey, and to whom exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could they be the novelist?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: We've thoroughly investigated that possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He claims to have spent the whole day at the opera house on the day of the murder, and the staff there have confirmed his account.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so he has an alibi...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Not only that, he lacks a credible motive as well.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: He has a family of his own and both of his parents are still alive. I've looked into his records... He was adopted at the age of six, and all the proper procedures were followed. There are also records of him at an orphanage before then.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: In the story, the mother of the two musketeers was murdered after the children turned ten. Of course, he could have changed the children's ages, but I don't want to assume anything without evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: More importantly, I've also had a chat with him in person. He didn't seem like the kind of person who would pull the trigger to kill a man.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then what should we do now? We have all this new information, but it doesn't help us move forward...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Investigations take time. I didn't expect us to catch the culprit in just a single day.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: How about this... Let's spend the next few days filming with the crew. We can continue the investigation once we're done with the film. I'm sure that given time, new leads will present themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, but weren't you saying intel is like "small, remote islands in the middle of the sea" just a moment ago? Wouldn't you just miss them if you were to stop looking?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Ah, but the book had more than one reference to the islands, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Oh? What else did it say then?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: "As long as you spend enough time sailing through the fog, you'll eventually come across an island."

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I don't need any help here, why don't you try asking someone else?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is what a musket looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Not exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Observe
dialogues.text: Some broken barrels and liquor bottles, some of which appear to have been shot with musket bullets.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's finally time to meet up with everyone! Paimon even dreamt of making the film last night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If Paimon remembers right, we're meeting at Hotel Debord. Let's get going!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So where are we going right now?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Let's start by checking out some workshops that sell mechanical components. If the culprit is making their own weapons, it's very likely that they'll visit those sort of places.
